reason: Paper 2 contributes a human-annotated reward benchmark, released reward models that beat open VLMs and match or exceed proprietary ones on it, and evidence that the reward enables stable Flow-GRPO training with gains on GEdit and ImgEdit, plus a useful analysis of reward variance. Paper 1 only benchmarks three existing distillation methods on noisy labels. It never compares against any noisy-label learning method, its privacy and 'vicious cycle' claims are untested, and its corollaries are informal and unproven. Paper 2 has weaknesses of its own: its training labels are distilled from GPT-4.1, its RL ablations are thin, and it reports no variance, but it remains far more substantive.
